description: Gold-standard baseline for self-hosted Next.js (App Router) applications running in Docker with PostgreSQL via Prisma 7, custom JWT auth (jose) and optional Python/Node sidecars. app-audit derives its score from `audit_checklist`; `deployment_checklist`, `anti_patterns` and `known_gotchas` are supporting evidence, not a second score. Edit `baseline_versions` to your own floors before the first run, and re-verify every floor against the vendor security page + OSV on each audit — versions rot.

baseline_versions._note: Placeholders. Set these to YOUR verified floors. A floor comes from an advisory range (OSV/GHSA) or a vendor security release, never from a blog post.
baseline_versions.nextjs_floor: <lowest patched Next.js version from the latest vendor security release>
baseline_versions.typescript: 5.9.x (TS 7 / ESLint 10 may not yet be supported by eslint-config-next — verify before bumping)
baseline_versions.prisma: 7.x pinned explicitly (never `prisma@latest` — the dist-tag can point at a release-candidate major)

runtime.node: Active-LTS Node on Alpine, SHA256 digest-pinned in every Dockerfile. Do not adopt a non-LTS 'Current' line.
runtime.nextjs: Tilde range (~X.Y.Z) on purpose — patch bumps only; a minor bump is a deliberate decision. Must be at or above the vendor security floor. Turbopack default, `next lint` removed (run eslint directly).
runtime.react: Pinned exactly; bump all apps together, not one by one.
runtime.typescript: 5.9.x. Confirm typescript-eslint supports a new TS major before adopting it.
runtime.python_sidecar: Digest-pinned slim base, 2-stage (builder venv -> runner), hash-pinned requirements.lock installed with --require-hashes, non-root uid 1001.
runtime.node_sidecar: 2-stage: builder `npm ci` + `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` (NodeNext, rewriteRelativeImportExtensions), runner `npm ci --omit=dev` + dist/ only, `node dist/...`. Never tsx in a production image.

database.postgresql: Digest-pinned postgres alpine image, one instance per app, never shared.
database.prisma: Prisma 7.x. The datasource block has no url; the url lives in prisma.config.ts.
database.adapter: @prisma/adapter-pg — MANDATORY for Prisma 7. Wired at RUNTIME in src/lib/prisma.ts: new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString, max, idleTimeoutMillis, connectionTimeoutMillis }) }). Never in prisma.config.ts.
database.pool: pg Pool config (max:10, min:2, idle:30s, connect:10s)
database.migrations_note: If an endpoint-protection product blocks Prisma's engine binary (`prisma migrate` -> spawn UNKNOWN), apply the migration SQL via psql inside BEGIN/COMMIT together with the _prisma_migrations row (checksum = sha256 of migration.sql). Back up (pg_dump -Fc) first.

cache.redis: Digest-pinned. Optional — an app without Redis must document it; rate limiting is then in-memory and durable lockout lives in the DB.
cache.auth: REQUIRED when present — password in REDIS_URL and REDIS_PASSWORD.

auth.primary: Custom HS256 JWT (jose 6.x). If several apps share an auth core, VENDOR it (copy via a sync script) rather than importing across build contexts, and never hand-edit a per-app copy.
auth.secret_validation: Fail-fast: min 32 chars, reject known weak/placeholder patterns
auth.lockout: Durable, fail-closed, on the users row: failedLoginAttempts + lockedUntil (5 attempts -> 15 min), guarded updateMany to survive races, lock decided BEFORE the password result is used so a locked account answers like a wrong password (timing + enumeration safe). lastLoginAt stamped on success.
auth.sessions: sessions.token stores sha256(jwt), never the raw JWT — a DB dump must not carry live sessions. Expired rows pruned best-effort on login.

validation.schema: zod 4. z.uuid() for route ids -> 400 before the DB; z.flattenError for 400 bodies.

testing.unit: Vitest 4.x/5.x. vitest.config.mts with tests/**/*.test.ts, node environment for lib + security-layer tests.
testing.e2e: Optional for a single-user local tool; verify UI in a real browser before claiming a page works.
testing.coverage: @vitest/coverage-v8 with thresholds ENFORCED in config so a drop fails `npm run test:coverage`. Floor 60 %; set a few points under the measured value once the app is properly tested. Prisma-heavy data layers are tested with the client mocked (vi.mock('@/lib/prisma')), not skipped.

ui.charts: recharts 3.x — eyeball charts after a major bump

ai.provider_switch: If the app calls an LLM: one client file dispatching on LLM_PROVIDER (see baselines/agents.json).
ai.host_services: Containers reach host-side services (local model server, LLM gateway) via host.docker.internal + `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway`. `localhost` inside a container is the container itself.

required_directories: src/app/ (App Router pages + API routes; a route group for the signed-in layout, login/ public)
src/app/api/ (request/response only — validation via src/lib validators, logic in src/lib)
src/lib/ (services, validators, logger, ratelimit, lockout, prisma.ts, auth.ts)
src/proxy.ts (Next.js 16 request proxy: rate limit, CSRF, JWT verify, nonce CSP, x-request-id) — or src/middleware.ts on older layouts
tests/ (vitest; lib logic + the security layer: proxy, lockout, ratelimit)
worker/ (sidecar where one exists: app/, tests/, Dockerfile, requirements.txt + requirements.lock)
database/init-app-user.sh (least-privilege app role created from env on first volume init)
required_root_files: Dockerfile (4-stage: base -> deps -> builder -> runner, apk upgrade in base, digest-pinned base)
docker-compose.yml (pinned /24 ipam subnet, 127.0.0.1 ports, ${VAR:?} for every secret)
prisma.config.ts (APP ROOT) — defineConfig({ schema, migrations, datasource: { url: env('DATABASE_URL') } })
next.config.ts (output 'standalone', poweredByHeader false, security headers; CSP per request in proxy.ts)
tsconfig.json (strict: true, target ES2022, module esnext, @/* alias)
.dockerignore (tests, docs, .env*, backups/, *.dump, *.sql, sidecar dirs — the context carries only what the image needs; NEVER tsconfig.json on @/* alias apps)
project_structure.structure_note: A flat src/lib with one file per concern is fine as long as route handlers stay thin (AP-NX-02).

authentication: Custom HS256 JWT (jose), algorithm pinned on verify
Zod validation on login input: email trimmed + lowercased, password min 1
Account lockout: 5 failed attempts -> 15 min, on the users row, fail-closed (a DB error = 500, never a session); locked account answers 401 like a wrong password
Unknown-email path runs bcrypt against a dummy cost-12 hash so timing does not reveal which emails exist
Password hashing bcryptjs cost 12 (never pass hashes through a shell — `$` gets expanded)
JWT_SECRET min 32 chars, weak/placeholder values rejected at first use
users.lastLoginAt stamped on success (+ session row with user agent / ip)
Session lookup key = sha256(jwt); expired sessions pruned on login
csrf: Origin/Host validation on all mutating requests (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), run BEFORE the public-route exemption so login-CSRF is covered
Reject missing Origin and `Origin: null` with 403 (never a 500) — fail closed
Exempt only /api/webhooks/*, /api/cron/*, API-key Bearer requests — where such routes exist
csp: Per-request nonce (16 random bytes, base64) on signed-in pages: script-src 'self' 'nonce-{n}' 'strict-dynamic'
Set on BOTH the request headers (Next reads the nonce there) and the response
Prerendered public pages (/login) may use 'unsafe-inline' instead of a nonce — document it
rate_limiting: Every /api/* route limited from ONE place (proxy.ts) so a per-route limiter cannot be forgotten: e.g. writes 60/min, reads 240/min per key; /api/health exempt
Login: 10/min per IP + 5/min per email inside the route
In-memory acceptable when the app has no Redis (documented); durable layer is the DB lockout
Forwarded-IP headers trusted ONLY when an explicit TRUST_PROXY=1 is set
encryption: Never store plaintext secrets in the database
docker: cap_drop: ALL + selective cap_add (CHOWN/DAC_OVERRIDE/FOWNER/SETGID/SETUID) for Postgres/Redis only
read_only: true on app AND worker + tmpfs for /tmp and .next/cache
Non-root user: uid 1001 in every image
All published ports bound to 127.0.0.1 unless deliberately public
Dedicated /24 subnet per app with PINNED ipam (an unpinned network can grab another stack's range)
Health checks on ALL services (127.0.0.1, never localhost) with service_healthy depends_on; app health route round-trips the DB
Resource limits: memory + cpus + pids on every container (deploy.resources.limits.pids)
Log rotation: json-file, max-size 10-50m, max-file 3-5, compress true
${VAR:?error} for every secret; `:-` only for non-secret feature toggles
Least-privilege DB role for the runtime (no CREATE); migrations as superuser
After any source change rebuild AND confirm `docker inspect <c> -f '{{.Image}}'` equals the tagged image id (--force-recreate on mismatch)
observability_ids: x-request-id generated in proxy.ts on EVERY request and always overwritten (a client must not choose it)
Every error/warn log in a route carries requestId + route (+ userId); login lines never carry email or password
sidecar: Every sidecar HTTP API is authenticated with a shared-secret header, compared timing-safe, fail-closed when unset; only /health open. 'Loopback only' is not a substitute — any local process can reach 127.0.0.1.
Upload routes refuse on declared content-length BEFORE buffering; zip uploads on DECLARED uncompressed size
Model/LLM replies parsed through a schema (zod / pydantic), never bare JSON.parse + property access

dockerfile.build_secrets: Placeholder AUTH_SECRET / DATABASE_URL for build-time `prisma generate` only

compose.healthchecks: app: wget /api/health, python worker: urllib /health, postgres: pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1, redis: redis-cli -a $REDIS_PASSWORD ping
compose.restart: unless-stopped for an app whose scheduled jobs must run unattended; 'no' is fine for an on-demand local tool. Document the choice in a compose comment.

docker.port_allocation: Each app claims unique app/db/worker ports + a /24 subnet; keep a registry (generated from the compose files, not hand-written). On Windows hosts, Hyper-V/winnat dynamic ranges can reserve any port — the durable fix is `netsh int ipv4 add excludedportrange`.

observability.logging: One JSON line per event on stdout (ts, level, msg, route, userId, requestId, err{name,message,code}); no request bodies or tokens
health_checks: App: GET /api/health round-trips Postgres (503 'degraded' when down) — a health check that cannot fail is not a check
operational: Scheduled/background jobs are checked in the DATA, not the logs: query the job table for the last 7 days and confirm runs complete. A 'healthy' container whose every scheduled run fails is a P1.
Unbounded tables need a retention rule — measure pg_total_relation_size per table
Cron-style routes need a scheduler AND a configured secret; a route waiting for a caller nobody set up is a dead feature. Verify in the data (last_run_at), never in `docker ps`.

prisma_client.file: src/lib/prisma.ts (one name fleet-wide; flag a reintroduced db.ts)
prisma_client.critical: ALL PrismaClient constructors use the PrismaPg adapter at runtime — including seeds
prisma_client.runtime_pattern: pg Pool + PrismaPg adapter + new PrismaClient({ adapter }); globalThis singleton in non-prod
prisma_client.build_guard: If DOCKER_BUILD is set, return a Proxy stub — `next build` collects page data without a DB
prisma_client.gotcha: DATABASE_URL uses 127.0.0.1, not localhost (IPv6 resolution on Alpine)

api_handler.pattern: export const POST = apiHandler(async (ctx) => { ... }, { schema, roles, rateLimit })

anti_patterns.name: Prisma 7 without adapter
anti_patterns.fix: Every PrismaClient() passes the PrismaPg adapter in src/lib/prisma.ts. prisma.config.ts only carries the datasource url for the CLI.

anti_patterns.name: Business logic in route handlers
anti_patterns.fix: Extract to src/lib — routes handle request/response only

anti_patterns.name: Single-condition mock auth
anti_patterns.fix: Triple-guard: NODE_ENV=development AND USE_MOCK_AUTH=true AND not a production URL

anti_patterns.name: console.log logging
anti_patterns.fix: Structured JSON logger with levels and correlation ids

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded secrets in Docker
anti_patterns.fix: Placeholders at build, real secrets via runtime env

anti_patterns.name: bcrypt hashes through shell
anti_patterns.fix: Pipe via Node stdin / execFile, never a shell string

anti_patterns.name: Port / subnet collision between stacks
anti_patterns.fix: Unique ports + pinned /24 per app; regenerate the registry from compose files

anti_patterns.name: Hardcoded LLM provider
anti_patterns.fix: Dispatch on LLM_PROVIDER; fail closed and loudly when the selected backend is unavailable

anti_patterns.name: Image pinned by tag alone
anti_patterns.fix: image:tag@sha256:<digest>; copy the digest from the registry API, never hand-type it

anti_patterns.name: Container running an older image than the one just built
anti_patterns.fix: Compare `docker inspect <c> -f '{{.Image}}'` with `docker images -q <image>`; --force-recreate on mismatch

anti_patterns.name: Scheduled job judged by container health instead of its own results
anti_patterns.fix: Audit the job table for the last 7 days

anti_patterns.name: Rolling daily quota spent by the first scheduled run
anti_patterns.fix: Split the daily cap across the day's slots (cap / slots per run)

anti_patterns.name: Append-only tables with no retention
anti_patterns.fix: Prune superseded progress rows (keep N days / newest per parent)

anti_patterns.name: prisma@latest / npm audit fix --force
anti_patterns.fix: Pin the 7.x range; never `npm audit fix --force` (it installs SemVer-major changes, sometimes downgrades)

anti_patterns.name: Missing extra_hosts for host services
anti_patterns.fix: `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway` on every service that calls a host-side service

good.name: Prisma 7 init
Auth secret validation
good.code: if (!secret || secret.length < 32 || KNOWN_WEAK.some(w => secret.includes(w))) throw new Error('FATAL: JWT_SECRET invalid');

good.name: Consistent response shape
good.code: return NextResponse.json({ data: items, pagination: { total, page, limit, pages } })

bad.name: Logic in route
bad.code: export async function POST(req) { const body = await req.json(); const item = await prisma.item.create({ data: body }); return NextResponse.json(item); }

bad.name: Prisma without adapter
bad.code: const prisma = new PrismaClient(); // BREAKS in Prisma 7

bad.name: No resource limits
bad.code: // compose service with no deploy.resources.limits — can OOM the host

deployment_checklist: output: 'standalone' and poweredByHeader: false in next.config.ts
4-stage Dockerfile with apk upgrade, digest-pinned base
Non-root uid 1001 in app and sidecar images
Health checks on every service; app route round-trips the DB
memory + cpus + pids limits on ALL containers
Log rotation (json-file, compress)
PrismaPg adapter in ALL PrismaClient constructors
Rate limiting on all API routes from proxy.ts (login 10/60s per IP + 5/60s per email)
CSRF Origin/Host check before the public-route exemption; webhook/cron/API-key exemptions where applicable
CSP with per-request nonce on signed-in pages
AES-256-GCM for stored third-party credentials (N/A when none stored)
Account lockout (5 / 15 min, DB row, fail-closed) + lastLoginAt
JWT secret validation (32+ chars, weak patterns rejected)
Security headers (X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS)
cap_drop ALL + no-new-privileges + read_only + tmpfs
All ports bound to 127.0.0.1
Dedicated pinned /24 subnet
Test coverage >= 60 % ENFORCED in vitest config
Python sidecar: digest-pinned base, hash-pinned requirements.lock
.env.example with openssl commands; .dockerignore excludes .env*, backups, dumps, tests
Running container image == built image after every rebuild
Scheduled jobs verified in their own table for the last 7 days
Retention for append-only / progress tables
In-range `npm outdated` wanted versions applied; majors ask-first; `npm audit` highs explained if dev-only with no fix

known_gotchas.issue: Prisma 7 removed url from the datasource block
known_gotchas.fix: prisma.config.ts with defineConfig() + PrismaPg adapter at runtime

known_gotchas.issue: Alpine resolves localhost to IPv6, breaking health checks
known_gotchas.fix: 127.0.0.1 in DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL and health checks

known_gotchas.issue: bcrypt `$` characters break when passed through a shell
Edge middleware cannot import Prisma or bcrypt
known_gotchas.fix: Keep the proxy/middleware edge-safe; DB work in route handlers

known_gotchas.issue: Linux containers cannot reach a host service at 127.0.0.1
Renaming the project root breaks bind mounts
known_gotchas.fix: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate` per stack; named volumes are safe

known_gotchas.issue: `AT TIME ZONE` on a naive timestamp goes the wrong way
known_gotchas.fix: (col AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE '<zone>' or convert in the app

known_gotchas.issue: Newer npm versions may skip unapproved install scripts
known_gotchas.fix: Packages with binaries (e.g. electron) install without their postinstall — approve the script or run it explicitly
Breaks @/* alias resolution in the Docker build — never exclude it (tsconfig.tsbuildinfo is fine)
Linux Docker builds fail on `rateLimit` vs `ratelimit` — match imports to the real file case

audit_checklist.note: PASS = 1, PARTIAL = 0.5, FAIL = 0. N/A items are excluded from the denominator. Quote file:line or command output for every non-PASS.

security.check: Custom JWT (jose) or equivalent vetted auth, algorithm pinned on verify; shared auth core (if any) unmodified vs its source
Zod validation on login and every API body; route ids validated as UUID (400)
Account lockout 5/15 min, durable (DB), fail-closed; locked account answers like a wrong password
JWT secret min 32 chars + weak-pattern rejection
CSRF Origin/Host check on all mutating requests incl. login; missing/null Origin -> 403
CSP per-request nonce + strict-dynamic on signed-in pages, frame-ancestors none, on request AND response
Rate limiting on every API route from one place; auth limits; 429 + Retry-After; forwarded IPs only behind TRUST_PROXY
AES-256-GCM for stored third-party credentials (N/A if none stored)
No hardcoded secrets: build placeholders, ${VAR:?} at runtime, .env excluded from image and context
Session tokens hashed at rest; expired rows pruned
Sidecar/worker API authenticated with a timing-safe shared-secret header, fail-closed; only /health open
Least-privilege DB role for the runtime (no CREATE); migrations as superuser
npm audit: 0 high/critical in runtime deps; framework at or above the VENDOR security floor (vendor advisories can precede OSV/GitHub DB)
Uploads refused on declared content-length before buffering; zip bombs on declared size

stack.check: Next.js at or above the configured floor, tilde range
Prisma 7 with PrismaPg adapter in src/lib/prisma.ts
prisma.config.ts at the app root with defineConfig + env('DATABASE_URL'); dotenv declared
npm outdated: no in-range 'wanted' updates pending

docker.check: Base images digest-pinned AND current (registry tag check)
Standalone output copied (standalone + static + public + prisma)
Health checks on all services at 127.0.0.1, service_healthy depends_on, app health round-trips DB
memory + cpus + pids limits on every container
cap_drop ALL + no-new-privileges; selective cap_add on PG/Redis only
read_only + tmpfs on app and worker
All ports 127.0.0.1 (or a documented, profile-gated public ingress)
Running container image == built image for every service
.dockerignore at every build context: no tests/docs/.env/dumps; tsconfig.json NOT excluded

testing.check: Security layer tested: proxy (CSRF, JWT, CSP, request id, limits), lockout, ratelimit
Tests under tests/, never next to source

observability.check: Structured JSON logger with levels; no bodies/tokens logged
x-request-id on every request and every route log line
App health round-trips DB; worker health too
Job status visible in the UI where the app runs jobs
Scheduled jobs succeeded in the last 7 days (query the job table)
No unexplained error-level lines in the app log for the last 48 h
Every cron-style route has a scheduler and a configured secret; data shows recent runs
